2027-07-22.title: Third Thursday of Kaitha · Saint Mary Magdalene
2027-07-22.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Who can separate us from the love of Christ?
Mary Magdalene proclaims the risen Christ
The prayer offered in faith will make the sick person well
Jesus sends out the twelve disciples
2027-07-22.alt: Season of Kaitha (Qaita, Summer), which began on Sunday 4 July with the Feast of the Twelve Apostles: the season of the Church's growth and harvest, when the Church remembers the apostles and martyrs who watered her field with their blood and keeps herself ready for the coming of the Lord. The calendar gives the readings of Saint Mary Magdalene and the weekday readings of the Third Thursday of Kaitha; both sets are shown here (verify locally which are read). The Latin Church keeps her feast today, and the Syro-Malankara Church keeps her memory.
2027-07-22.verse: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord”; and she told them that he had said these things to her.
theo: Of all the women who followed Jesus, one is named in every Gospel: Mary of Magdala, a town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee. Luke tells us who she was before the Lord met her: “Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out”, who with Joanna, Susanna and many others “provided for them out of their resources” (Luke 8:2–3). A woman who had been delivered from a great darkness spent the rest of her life giving back what she had received. We know her only through what the Gospels say: her healing, her service, her courage. She is among the women who watched “from a distance” (Mark 15:40), and John puts her “near the cross of Jesus”, standing with his mother (John 19:25). She saw where the body was laid (Mark 15:47). The Gospels do not say that she was the sinful woman of Luke 7 or Mary of Bethany; the Church today keeps these women distinct, and the older identification made in the Western Church is remembered only as a tradition, which the Eastern Churches never adopted. What the Gospels give is enough: she is the disciple who stayed when others fled.

Her whole story is an answer to the question of today's Epistle: “Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Will hardship, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?” Paul's answer is a cry of victory: “No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us. For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.” Mary Magdalene did not read these lines, but she lived them. Not the soldiers, not the darkness, not even the closed tomb could separate her from the love she had received. Many Christians have heard in her search the voice of the bride in the Song of Songs: “I will seek him whom my soul loves” (Song of Songs 3:2).

John tells the Easter morning with a care that makes us see it: “Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed.” She runs to Simon Peter and the beloved disciple; they run to the tomb, see the linen wrappings, and the beloved disciple believes, and then “the disciples returned to their homes.” “But Mary stood weeping outside the tomb.” The angels ask, “Woman, why are you weeping?” and then the Lord himself, whom she does not recognise, asks the same question and adds, “Whom are you looking for?” She takes him for the gardener: “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.” She will carry the body of the Lord herself if she must. Then comes the shortest and greatest speech in the Gospel: “Jesus said to her, ‘Mary!’ She turned and said to him in Hebrew, ‘Rabbouni!’ (which means Teacher).” The Good Shepherd calls his own sheep by name (John 10:3), and she knows his voice. He is not recognised by his face but by the way he says her name.

Then the risen Lord gives her a mission: “Do not hold on to me, because I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’” She must not cling to the old way of being near him; a new nearness is coming, through the Ascension and the Spirit. And for the first time he calls the disciples “my brothers” and shares his Father with them. “Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, ‘I have seen the Lord’.” Luke records how her message was received: the words seemed to the apostles “an idle tale” (Luke 24:11). Yet the Church's whole witness begins with her voice. This is why Saint Thomas Aquinas called her the apostle of the apostles, and why in 2016 the Church raised her memorial to a feast. In the Season of Kaitha, which honours the apostles, the Church places beside the Twelve the woman whom the Lord himself sent to tell the Twelve. The Eastern Churches honour her among the myrrh-bearing women who came to the tomb with their ointments.

The weekday readings, too, speak of prayer and mission. James teaches the prayer of the community: “Are any among you suffering? They should pray. Are any cheerful? They should sing songs of praise.” He mentions the anointing of the sick with oil, confession to one another, and the prayer of the righteous, which “is powerful and effective”: “Elijah was a human being like us, and he prayed fervently”. The prophet whom the Syro-Malankara Church remembered on Tuesday is held up as a man like us, so that we may pray as he did. The Gospel is the sending of the Twelve: “As you go, proclaim the good news, ‘The kingdom of heaven has come near.’ ... You received without payment; give without payment.” “As you enter the house, greet it. If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it.” Mary Magdalene received without payment, from the Lord who drove out the seven demons, and she gave without payment, all she had. She entered the room of the frightened disciples with the first greeting of Easter on her lips. Today we ask for the same love that does not leave, the same ears that know his voice, and the same courage to announce, “I have seen the Lord.”
outline: A woman delivered from darkness who stayed when others fled.
Point 1 · Love that is not separated
At the cross and at the tomb; nothing in creation can separate us from the love of Christ.
She seeks and weeps; the Good Shepherd calls his sheep by name.
Point 3 · Do not hold on, but go
A new nearness and a mission: “go to my brothers”.
“I have seen the Lord”: the first witness, and the word that was thought an idle tale.
live: Visit this week someone who is suffering or who is alone, and simply stay near them, as Mary stayed near the cross.
Each morning this week, after your prayer, stay silent for a minute and listen for the Lord calling you by name; then go and tell one person something good that you have seen of him.
fathers: Mary stayed at the tomb to seek him whom she had not found, and because she went on seeking she found him. So her desire grew by waiting, and by growing it became able to receive what it found.
She is rightly called the apostle of the apostles, for she announced to the apostles what they were to announce to the world.
magis: Mary Magdalene and the holy women, who came to anoint the body of Jesus, were the first to encounter the Risen One; so women were the first messengers of Christ's Resurrection to the apostles themselves.
The empty tomb is a first sign, not a proof; the apostles come to believe in the Resurrection through the encounter with the Risen Lord, and Mary Magdalene is the first to meet him.
The risen body of Jesus is the same body that was crucified, yet it shares in the divine life; so he appears as he wishes and is not recognised at once, as Mary Magdalene took him for the gardener.
saints: Saint Mary Magdalene, disciple of the Lord and first witness of the Resurrection, called “apostle of the apostles”. The Latin Church has kept her feast since 2016, and the Syro-Malankara Church keeps her memory today; the Eastern Churches honour her among the myrrh-bearing women.

19–24 July: the third week of Kaitha. Mon 19 to Wed 21 and Sat 24: the Third Week of Kaitha, with the Epistle from the Letter of James (Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat). Thu 22: Saint Mary Magdalene, apostle of the apostles, with readings of her own. Fri 23: the Third Friday of Kaitha (readings from the 2022–23 calendar, verify locally). Sat 24: in the Latin and Malankara calendars, Saint Sharbel Makhluf, a monk of the Maronite Church. Looking ahead: the Fourth Sunday of Kaitha on 25 July, and Saint Alphonsa on Wednesday 28 July.
2027-07-22.prayer: Risen Lord Jesus Christ, you called Mary Magdalene by her name in the garden and sent her to your brothers. Call us by name, and make us hear your voice. Give us her love that stayed at the cross and her courage that sought you in the dark. Let nothing in creation separate us from your love, and make us witnesses who can say, “I have seen the Lord.” Hear us through the prayers of Saint Mary Magdalene, apostle of the apostles, for you live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, one God, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the risen Lord is present, and he calls each of us by name as he called Mary in the garden. We do not hold on to him as Mary tried to do; he gives himself to us in the Bread and the Cup and then sends us, as he sent her, to tell our brothers and sisters, “I have seen the Lord.”

quick: Mary Magdalene was healed by the Lord, served him, stood near the cross with his mother, and came to the tomb in the dark; the risen Lord called her by name and sent her to the apostles.
Paul: nothing in creation can separate us from the love of Christ; James: pray in suffering, praise in joy, confess and be healed; Matthew: the Twelve are sent to proclaim and to bring peace.
Together: love that stays, a name that is called, and a mission to tell.
2027-07-22.action: Go to someone who is suffering and stay near them, then tell one person that you have seen the Lord at work.
2027-07-22.question: Where is the Lord calling me by name, and whom must I tell?
kidsaint: Mary Magdalene was a friend and follower of Jesus. Jesus had made her well, and she loved him very much. When Jesus died she stayed near the cross. On Easter morning, while it was still dark, she went to the tomb and cried because she could not find Jesus. Then someone said her name: “Mary!” It was Jesus, alive! He asked her to go and tell his friends, and she ran to tell them: “I have seen the Lord!” Lesson: Jesus calls each of us by name. Stay near him, and tell others the good news!
term: A title given to Saint Mary Magdalene since the early centuries and by Saint Thomas Aquinas, because the risen Lord sent her to announce the Resurrection to the apostles. The word apostle means one who is sent. In 2016 the Church raised her memorial to a feast.

family.explain: Mary was crying outside the empty tomb because she could not find Jesus. Then Jesus said just one word: “Mary!” and she knew his voice at once. He told her to go to his friends and tell them the good news, and she ran and said: “I have seen the Lord!” God knows each of us by name, and he sends us to tell good news too.
family.intention: We thank God for calling us by name at baptism, and we pray for all who are sad or lonely today.
family.ask: Ask: “What good news can we tell someone in our village or school this week?”

illus: In a parish near Pala (a story told to illustrate the reading) a widow named Annamma came every day before dawn to sweep the church courtyard and light the lamp, long before the first bell. When asked why she came in the dark, she said, ‘On the first Easter someone came while it was still dark. I want to be there when he calls my name.’ On Easter morning the children found her kneeling with the lamp at the open door, and the old priest began the Easter greeting by naming her first: ‘Annamma, the Lord is risen.’ She answered, as the parish does, ‘He is risen indeed,’ and went to tell the whole village.

pm.open: Risen Lord, you called Mary by name in the garden. Call us by name too, and let us hear your voice as we gather. Amen.
share: Who will separate us from the love of Christ? (Romans 8:35). What do I fear might separate me from him?
Mary stood weeping outside the tomb (John 20:11). Where do I stand and weep, and what am I looking for?
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” (John 20:16). How does the Lord call me by name?
Go to my brothers and say to them (John 20:17). To whom does the Lord send me, and what shall I say?
pm.resp: Lord, we have seen you; send us.
interc: For the Church, that she may always proclaim the Resurrection with the courage of Saint Mary Magdalene.
For women who serve the Church in quiet ways, that their witness may be valued and their gifts used.
For those who weep because they cannot find the Lord, that he may call them by name.
For the sick and those who are anointed in this season of rains and fevers, that the prayer of faith may heal them.
For ourselves, that we may stay near the Lord in the dark and tell others what we have seen.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and sent Mary Magdalene to tell his brothers. Make us faithful witnesses of the Resurrection, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today the Church remembers Saint Mary Magdalene. The Lord healed her of great darkness, and she followed him to the end. She stood near the cross with Mary his mother, and on Easter morning, while it was still dark, she came to the tomb (John 20:1).

She found the tomb empty and she wept. And then someone said her name: “Mary!” (John 20:16). That is all it took. She knew his voice. The Good Shepherd knows each sheep by name, and he knows you by your name.

Then Jesus gave her work: “go to my brothers and say to them...” (John 20:17). “Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, ‘I have seen the Lord’” (John 20:18). The apostles at first thought it an idle tale, but this woman was the first witness of the Resurrection. That is why the Church calls her the apostle of the apostles.

Saint Paul asks, “Who will separate us from the love of Christ?” (Romans 8:35). Not hardship, not death, not the darkness. Mary did not let go of her love at the cross, and she was the first to see the risen Lord.
This week let us stay near the Lord when it is dark, listen for him calling our name, and tell at least one person what he has done for us. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know the friend of Jesus who cried at the empty tomb? It was Mary Magdalene. She missed Jesus so much! Then Jesus called her name, “Mary!”, and she knew it was him. She ran to tell everyone: “I have seen the Lord!” Jesus knows your name too. Tell someone this week about how good Jesus is!

intro: Theme: “Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, ‘I have seen the Lord’.”
The love that is not separated, the name that is called, the mission “go to my brothers”, and the apostle of the apostles.

sub: At the cross, with the mother of Jesus.
At the tomb, in the dark.
Nothing in all creation can separate us.
q: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is strong as death, passion fierce as the grave.

For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
points.apply: Stay near someone who is suffering this week.

sub: The Good Shepherd calls by name.
Known by the voice, not by the face.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher).
points.apply: Listen each morning for the Lord calling you by name.

points.h: Do not hold on, but go
sub: A new nearness through the Ascension.
The mission is entrusted to a woman.
q: I will tell of your name to my brothers and sisters; in the midst of the congregation I will praise you:
Jesus said to her, “Do not hold on to me, because I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”
points.apply: Tell one person this week something good that the Lord has done for you.

sub: An idle tale to the Twelve.
The Church's witness begins with her voice.
q: I shall not die, but I shall live, and recount the deeds of the Lord.
Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord”; and she told them that he had said these things to her.
points.apply: Be a witness in your home this week: say aloud where you have seen the Lord.

concl: Saint Mary Magdalene stayed when others fled, heard her name, and was sent to tell the Twelve.
The Lord calls us by name and sends us to our brothers and sisters, to say what we have seen.
2027-07-22.resolve: This week, stay near one who suffers, listen for your name, and tell someone, “I have seen the Lord.”
